# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)

**RE:** Reese Iverson, Member ID W233165693
**Reference Number:** POC-757C3B7E16-21498
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-06
**Governing Policy:** Carelon Joint Surgery 2025-11-15 (HTML), https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/ (effective 2025-11-15)

Dear Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), as stated in the notice dated 2026-08-06, reference number POC-757C3B7E16-21498. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## The Stated Reason for Denial

The denial states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I want to address this directly, and I also want to be clear about what I can and cannot verify from the plan's own published criteria.

## What the Plan's Policy Excerpts Show

The excerpts of the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline that I have been given address shoulder **arthroplasty** — for example, the guideline states that "shoulder arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications," and separately sets out criteria for hemiarthroplasty, reverse shoulder arthroplasty, and "Revision or Replacement of a Shoulder Prosthesis." These are joint-replacement procedures, not rotator cuff repair. I have not been given, and cannot locate in the material provided to me, the specific section of the guideline that sets out the plan's conservative-care requirements for rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827). Because I have not been quoted the section of the policy that actually governs this procedure, I am not able to show word-for-word how my records meet it — and I want to be transparent about that rather than quote language that does not apply to my case.

That said, I believe my records demonstrate a substantial and adequately documented trial of conservative treatment, regardless of which specific duration threshold the plan applies:

- **Symptom duration:** 18 months of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Physical therapy:** 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, from 2026-02-24 to 2026-06-16, with 16 visits completed and documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** A corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-30, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging:** MRI on 2026-07-07 showing a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- **Function and exam:** I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side, and my exam showed positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion on the affected side.

These records show months of guideline-consistent, supervised conservative treatment — physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication, and an injection — that did not resolve my symptoms, alongside imaging confirming a structural tear that my surgeon has determined requires repair.

## Request That the Plan Provide the Applicable Criteria in Writing

Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana uses Carelon to review musculoskeletal surgery requests, and Carelon publishes its clinical guidelines publicly, without a login requirement. Because the criteria applied to deny my request do not appear to match the rotator cuff repair section of the guideline, I am asking the plan to identify, and provide to me in writing, the exact section and language of the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline (or any other guideline) that it applied in reviewing this request for CPT 29827, including the specific conservative-care duration or documentation requirement it found unmet.

## Conclusion and Request

I am asking the plan to reconsider this denial in light of the conservative treatment I completed and the imaging findings confirming a full-thickness rotator cuff tear, and to provide the specific policy criteria used to evaluate my request. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-02. I will send this appeal to the address listed on my denial notice, or, if that is not available to me, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Thank you for your attention to this appeal. Please contact me if you need any additional information from me or from Dr. Duval's office.

Sincerely,

________________________
Reese Iverson
Member ID: W233165693
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [Date of submission]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

quotes: shoulder arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:

Limited range of motion or crepitus of the glenohumeral joint on physical examination Pain and loss of function of at least 6 months’ duration that interferes with daily activities (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4) *Radiographic evidence of destructive degenerative joint disease as evidenced by marked joint space narrowing AND ONE or more of the following:

Irregular joint surfaces Glenoid sclerosis Osteophyte changes Flattened glenoid Cystic changes in the humeral head Failure of conservative management of at least 6 weeks’ duration (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 or diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III-IV changes) Hemiarthroplasty Hemiarthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:

Proximal humerus fracture confirmed by imaging not amenable to internal fixation (e.g., severe comminution, poor bone quality, multi-part, displaced) Malignancy involving the glenohumeral joint or surrounding soft tissue Advanced joint disease of the shoulder when criteria for total shoulder arthroplasty are met AND at least ONE of the following conditions is present:

Osteonecrosis of the humeral head without glenoid involvement Glenoid bone stock inadequate to support a glenoid prosthesis Advanced joint disease due to rotator cuff tear arthropathy* Glenohumeral osteoarthritis with irreparable rotator cuff tear* *except for Exclusions listed below Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty Reverse shoulder arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:

Deficient rotator cuff with limited ability to actively flex the upper extremity above the plane of the shoulder Revision or Replacement of a Shoulder Prosthesis Revision or replacement of a shoulder prosthesis is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions when associated with pain and functional impairment:
Preoperative investigation using serologic testing and IF there are abnormal laboratory findings, at least ONE of the following:

Synovial fluid testing, such as leukocyte count and neutrophil percentage, aerobic and anaerobic bacterial cultures, leukocyte esterase, alpha defensin testing (Synovasure®), synovial fluid CRP, synovial fluid PCR for bacteria Intraoperative plan for histopathology and/or aerobic and anaerobic tissue cultures using implant sonication for cultures or PCR Contraindications All procedures listed in this guideline are contraindicated when ANY of the following conditions are present:

Active infection of the joint Active systemic bacteremia Active skin infection or open wound at the surgical site Rapidly progressive neurologic disease Intra-articular corticosteroid injection within the past 6 weeks in the joint being replaced Exclusions Indications other than those addressed in this guideline are considered not medically necessary including, but not limited to, the following:

Shoulder arthroplasty under conditions which would result in excessive stress on the implant including, but not limited to, Charcot joint and paralytic conditions of the shoulder Shoulder resurfacing, including total, hemi, or partial resurfacing (e.g., Copeland™, the Extended Articulating Surface (EAS)™ Resurfacing Heads, Global CAP™ CTA Resurfacing Shoulder Humeral Head)
